learningObjective: Compare PyTorch Profiler with Nsight Systems/Compute and choose the appropriate tool for a given debugging task.

canonicalClaims.claim: The three profilers occupy distinct roles: PyTorch Profiler for op-level attribution (which Python/aten op launched which kernel), Nsight Systems for system-level tracing (CPU/GPU/PCIe/library), and Nsight Compute for per-kernel deep-dive metrics.
conditions: The user is debugging a specific class of issue (op attribution, system-level, kernel-internal).
nonImplications: Does not imply one tool subsumes the others.
Does not imply the tools always agree numerically.

misconceptions.claim: Nsight Systems shows per-kernel warp stall reasons.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Warp stall reasons are Nsight Compute's domain.

misconceptions.claim: PyTorch Profiler exposes per-kernel SM utilization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PyTorch Profiler stops at CUDA kernel launch attribution; kernel-internal metrics come from Nsight Compute.

misconceptions.claim: The three tools produce identical measurements.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Different sampling and instrumentation lead to slightly different numbers.

misconceptions.claim: Using all three is always necessary for any performance issue.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Simple issues (missing sync, obvious launch overhead) often need only one tool.
